WHO ARE WE?

Cohere is the leading security-first enterprise AI company.  We build cutting-edge foundation AI models and end-to-end products that are designed to solve real-world business problems.

We’re training and deploying frontier models for enterprises who are building AI systems. We believe that our work is instrumental to the widespread adoption of AI and we are looking for folks that want to be part of that.

We obsess over what we build. Each one of us is responsible for contributing to increasing the capabilities of our models and the value they drive for our customers. Cohere is a team of researchers, engineers, designers, and more, who are all passionate about their craft.

We are a global technology company headquartered in Toronto with key offices in London, New York City, San Francisco, Montreal, Paris, Berlin and Seoul. Join us!




ABOUT THE ROLE

We're looking for a design engineer to help build and maintain Waypoint, our design system, across both the Figma library and the production codebase. This is not a "designer who codes a little" or an "engineer who dabbles in Figma" role. You should be genuinely fluent on both sides, comfortable defining a component's behavior and states in Figma one hour and shipping the same component to npm the next.

You'll take direct ownership of the Figma side of our library (structure, variants, tokens, documentation) while also contributing to the core Waypoint system: our component packages, our token pipeline, and the tooling that keeps design and code in sync. If the idea of being the single point of continuity between a Figma frame and a production component sounds exciting rather than exhausting, this is your role.

We're also thinking beyond the system we have today. Waypoint isn't just meant to serve designers and engineers, it's meant to become something a model can read, reason about, and build with directly. We want someone who can help us get there: grounded enough to do the unglamorous work of making today's system solid, and forward looking enough to help define what an intelligent design system looks like next.



WHY THIS ROLE

Waypoint is still early enough that the decisions you make now will shape how the system scales. You'll have real ownership, not just a queue of component tickets, and you'll be working alongside a team that treats design and engineering as one discipline rather than two departments that hand work back and forth. And you'll be helping define what a design system becomes when it has to serve a third audience: the models that will increasingly build with it.




RESPONSIBILITIES

 - Own and evolve the Figma library for Waypoint: component structure, variants, properties, and documentation, so it stays a reliable source of truth for design teams.

 - Build and maintain core Waypoint components, contributing directly to our component packages alongside the design engineering team.

 - Work across our token pipeline, keeping design tokens in Figma and their code representations (CSS custom properties, Tailwind config) tightly synced.

 - Partner with product designers to translate new patterns into system components, and with product engineers to make sure those components are easy to adopt correctly.

 - Help define and refine the workflows and tooling that connect Figma and code (sync scripts, plugins, documentation sites) rather than relying on manual handoff.

 - Write clear documentation and usage guidance so the system scales without you being the bottleneck.

 - Weigh in on system architecture decisions: when to add a new component versus extend an existing one, how to version and package changes, how to keep the system consistent as it grows.

 - Help shape how Waypoint evolves to serve a third consumer beyond designers and engineers: the model itself. That means thinking about how components, tokens, and patterns get structured so they're legible to AI systems, not just to humans.




QUALIFICATIONS

 - 6+ years of combined design and/or engineering experience, with real depth in both. We care less about your job titles and more about whether you can move fluidly between Figma and code without losing fidelity in either direction.

 - Strong command of Figma at a systems level: component architecture, variants, auto layout, variables and tokens, and library management, not just using components someone else built.

 - Solid front end engineering skills, ideally TypeScript and React, with the ability to build accessible, well tested, production quality components.

 - Experience working with or building design tokens and understanding how they flow from design tool to codebase.

 - A systems mindset. You think in terms of reusable, composable patterns rather than one off solutions, and you can explain the tradeoffs of a system level decision to both designers and engineers.

 - Strong communication skills. You'll be the connective tissue between design and engineering, so you need to be able to advocate for system decisions to both audiences.

 - Comfort with ambiguity. Design systems work means constantly balancing consistency against the need to move fast and support new product surfaces.

 - A genuine interest in where design systems are headed, not just where they are. You should be able to hold the practical reality of today's system alongside a point of view on what it means to build for a future where AI is a first class consumer of your system, not just an afterthought.

 


NICE-TO-HAVES

 - Experience building or contributing to design-to-code sync tooling (Figma plugins, token pipelines, MCP-based workflows, or similar).

 - Familiarity with accessibility standards (WCAG) and how to bake them into components rather than bolt them on.

 - Experience packaging and versioning component libraries for multiple consuming teams (npm scoped packages, semver, changelogs).

 - Exposure to multi-platform design systems work (iOS/SwiftUI, Android/Jetpack Compose, or token build tools like Style Dictionary).

 - Experience in an AI native product environment or genuine interest in how AI changes the way design systems get built and used.




FULL-TIME EMPLOYEES AT COHERE ENJOY THESE PERKS:

 - A weekly lunch stipend of $75/£75 or equivalent in your local currency for lunch.

 - Full health and dental benefits, including a separate budget for mental health.

 - RRSP matching, 401K, Pension Scheme.

 - 100% Parental Leave top-up for up to 6 months, for either parent.

 - Annual enrichment benefits:
   
   Arts & culture, fitness/wellness, quality time, and a workspace improvement credit.
   
   Education & learning stipend for conferences, courses, and coaching.

 - 6 weeks of paid vacation (30 working days!)

 - Budget for traveling to other offices if you are remote, plus an annual company offsite.




HOW AND WHERE WE WORK:

 - Cohere is remote-friendly, but we also have offices in Toronto, London, New York City, San Francisco, Montreal, Paris, Berlin and Seoul with more opening soon.

 - For those in the office: a daily lunch program, plenty of snacks, and regular community and social events.

 - For those not near an office: a co-working benefit so you can work alongside others in your city.

 - Everyone receives a $500 home office stipend to set up your workspace properly.
   
   

If any of the above doesn’t line up exactly with your experience, we still encourage you to apply. 


We strive to create an inclusive work environment for all; we welcome applicants from all backgrounds and are committed to providing equal opportunities. Should you require any accommodations during the recruitment process, please submit an Accommodations Request Form https://docs.google.com/forms/d/12a6IrLdF3kI2nonKSr4tiFuz18rLQbaeYV-JM9L4o9Q/edit, and we will work together to meet your needs.



We may use AI-enabled tools to screen and assess applicants against the criteria for this position. This helps our recruiters identify potentially qualified candidates, but it doesn't limit the applications our recruiters may review or consider.



Beware of Scams: Cohere will never ask for payment or third-party services (e.g., CV writing) as part of our hiring process. All legitimate roles are listed on the Cohere careers page and LinkedIn only, with all communications from Cohere employees coming from an @cohere.com or @cw.cohere email alias. If jobs are viewed on other sites then please verify these through our official careers https://cohere.com/careers page.

Hi 👋🏻 I’m Louis, Head of Security. You’ll report directly to me.

What Ashby gives you in return is the best of both early and growth-stage environments. The agency and no-nonsense of a seed startup: you contribute to useful projects, make practical decisions, and work in an almost-no-meeting culture. The product-market fit and scale of a growth-stage startup: tens of thousands of daily users who depend on our software, and customers whose trust your work will help us earn.

We have notable customers like Notion, Linear, Shopify, and Snowflake. Our growth and retention metrics are best-in-class among our peers: we have tens of millions in ARR, growing >100% year over year, very low churn, and many years of runway. We’ll share more details once we meet.

You’ll join our Security team, a single team with multiple specializations overseeing security across the business. I report to Abhik, our Co-Founder and VP of Engineering. We’re bubbling with ideas on how to support Talent Acquisition through software, and we’ve started the journey of building products beyond Talent Acquisition. We read every application and aim to respond to yours within 3-4 days (often sooner).




ROLE OVERVIEW

We’re looking for an engineer with a passion to learn whose focus is on building “paved roads” specifically around making secure delivery part of the way we build and ship software. You’ll operate the checks and workflows around our delivery pipeline, help engineers act on useful findings, and make routine exceptions straightforward under agreed policies.

We expect you to bring the same care to the reliability of a security check and the time it costs an engineer as you bring to the risk it addresses. You’ll build the integrations, learn from rollout, and maintain what you ship.

We have notable customers like Notion, Linear, Shopify, and Snowflake. Our growth and retention metrics are best-in-class among our peers: we have tens of millions in ARR, growing >100% year over year, over 2500 customers, very low churn, and many years of runway. We’ll share more details once we meet, but you now probably have a good idea as to why we're hiring for this role 😅.




ABOUT THE ROLE AND HOW WE WORK

We’re also advertising this opening as Senior Security Platform Engineer - Secure Delivery. Both titles describe the same position; please apply once using the title that best reflects your experience.

Your mission is to make our delivery pipeline secure by default across application code, infrastructure, dependencies, containers, and product configuration. You’ll own the technical implementation and operation of delivery-security tooling and controls, including integration, configuration, tuning, reliability, and coverage.

Product Engineering teams own triage and remediation for the features they maintain. Application Security provides specialist analysis and defines product-security test requirements. Infrastructure retains ownership of the underlying cloud platform. You’ll work with those teams to make agreed checks and policies run reliably in the delivery workflow.

In practice, you’ll:

 - Deploy, configure, integrate, and tune static analysis, dependency, secret, container, and Infrastructure as Code scanning in our CI/CD workflows.

 - Inventory production repositories and delivery paths, including prompts and model configuration. Make scanner coverage distinct from application-specific tests of AI behavior; AppSec defines those tests, and you operate agreed delivery checks.

 - Start new checks in report-only mode where appropriate, then implement agreed warn and block policies using exploitability, exposure, and compensating controls.

 - Give engineers self-service exceptions within documented rules, with an owner, justification, expiry, and audit trail. Escalate decisions outside those rules to Security leadership with the relevant specialist analysis.

 - Build automation and AI-assisted workflows that enrich findings, propose fixes, and support Product Engineering’s triage under documented criteria. Preserve required checks, review, and rollback for automated patch changes.

 - Make coverage, integration failures, finding age by risk, time to triage and remediate, false blocks, build delay, and bypasses visible. Record mitigations separately from completed fixes and connect useful telemetry to GRC evidence.

 - Work with Infrastructure on cloud-posture monitoring, useful critical-misconfiguration alerts, and bounded remediation automation.

 - Extend into shared-image hardening and artifact provenance as the delivery foundations mature.

To ground it with examples, you could:

 - Roll out secret scanning with push protection and make a blocked push understandable and actionable for an engineer.

 - Turn a repeated scanner-exception request into a PR workflow with a reason, expiry, and evidence for revisiting it.

 - Reproduce a dependency issue in the application, add a regression check, and build a workflow that proposes a patch with useful evidence.

 - Show which delivery paths are covered, where checks fail, and whether enforcement is addressing risk while keeping build delays reasonable.




WHY YOU SHOULD AND SHOULDN’T APPLY

You’ve built and operated CI/CD, developer tooling, or infrastructure automation used by other engineers. You can write maintainable code, explain the failure modes of what you shipped, and use security evidence to make a practical rollout decision. Supply-chain and scanner experience is useful; you can learn individual tools as part of the work.

You’ve applied AI in engineering and can explain how you check its outputs and permissions. You enjoy treating engineers as users, making build-versus-buy decisions, and improving adoption and reliability after launch.

You might not enjoy the role if:

 - You prefer to deliver a prototype and hand off its operation. Reliability, tuning, and existing integrations are part of the work.

 - You prefer a prescribed backlog to investigating an ambiguous problem, writing a proposal, and bringing partners into the work.

 - You want standalone assessments to be your main output. This role centers on working delivery capabilities and their adoption.
   


INTERVIEW PROCESS

If this also sounds exciting to you, please apply. We review every application and aim to get back to candidates within 2-3 days. For candidates who advance to the interview process, here is what you can expect:

 - Recruiter Screen - 30 mins

 - Hiring Manager Intro Call - 20 mins

 - Past Projects Deep Dive - 45 mins

 - Founder Screening - 45 mins

 - Take-Home Assessment +  Practical Assessment Review - 1 hr (2-3 spent on take-home assignment)

 - Cross-Functional Stakeholder Interview - 45 mins




ROLE-SPECIFIC TECHNOLOGY AND TOOLS

For this role, CI/CD and infrastructure automation experience matter more than familiarity with a particular scanner. GitHub Actions or comparable systems, Terraform, containers, and cloud controls are relevant. You should be comfortable writing production automation in TypeScript, Python, Go, or a comparable language. Tool choices and individual scanner integrations are part of the work.




YOUR FIRST THREE MONTHS AT ASHBY

Your early changes will give you a tour of our codebase, infrastructure, and best practices, increasing in scope and ambiguity as you learn how we work. You’ll pair program with your onboarding peer as you learn the delivery workflows.

Your initial focus will be to:

 - Map production delivery paths and gaps across code, infrastructure, prompts, configuration, and evals, with clear ownership of the different checks.

 - Deliver a bounded scanning integration, such as secret push protection or report-only static analysis, with a usable finding workflow.

 - Establish initial warn, block, and self-service exception rules with the relevant partners and make Product Engineering ownership visible.

 - Baseline coverage, integration failures, false blocks, and build delay so the next rollout has evidence to build on.

Early progress means engineers can use the selected checks, act on their findings, and handle routine exceptions. Broader rollout follows the agreed risk policy and what the first integration teaches us.




BENEFITS

 - Competitive salary and equity.

 - 10-year exercise window for stock options. You shouldn’t feel pressure to purchase stock options if you leave Ashby —do it when you feel financially comfortable.

 - Unlimited PTO, and we will encourage you to take it.

 - A minimum of 12 weeks of fully paid parental leave, covered by Ashby. The actual number may increase to satisfy local requirements.

 - Generous equipment, software, and office furniture budget. Get what you need to be happy and productive!

 - $100/month education budget with more expensive items (like conferences) covered with manager approval.

 - If you’re in the US, we offer top-tier health insurance for you and your dependents, with 100% of premiums covered by Ashby. In other countries, we provide high-quality supplemental health insurance for you and your dependents, also fully covered by us.




CLOSING

Ashby’s success hinges on hiring great people and creating an environment where we can be happy, feel challenged, and do our best work. We’re being deliberate about building that environment from the ground up. I hope that excites you enough to apply.

Ashby provides equal employment opportunities (EEO) to all employees and applicants for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, genetics, sexual orientation, gender identity, or gender expression. We are committed to a diverse and inclusive workforce and welcome people from all backgrounds, experiences, perspectives, and abilities.

Position Title:   Mobile Outreach Worker 
 Competition: 26-060
 Reports to:  Manager of Supportive Housing 
 Union:  BCGEU
 Compensation:   $27.86-$30.26/hour
 Schedule:  8:00am - 7:00pm, Thursday to Saturday and every other Wednesday (70 hours bi-weekly)
 Posting Closing Date: November 15, 2026 at 4pm
 Position’s Primary Objectives: 
 The Mobile Outreach Worker provides individualized, person-centered support to tenants of Pacifica Housing across multiple sites and within the community. This role is designed to meet tenants where they are, extending flexible, mobile, and ongoing support services that promote housing stability, health, and overall quality of life. Guided by a harm reduction and Housing First philosophy, Mobile Outreach Workers help tenants address barriers such as mental health challenges, substance use, poverty, and social isolation while fostering resilience, autonomy, and community connection.
 Mobile Outreach Workers are accountable for delivering comprehensive services that may include advocacy, crisis intervention, life skills development, health navigation, and support with financial or tenancy-related responsibilities. They also provide backup to site staff, respond to emergencies including overdoses, and act as a key connector between tenants and external community resources. By building meaningful, professional relationships and supporting tenants in achieving their individualized goals, Mobile Outreach Workers contribute to safer, healthier, and more inclusive communities.
 Key Responsibilities: 
 Tenant Support & Advocacy 
 Transport, support, and advocate alongside tenants at community appointments (e.g., Ministry services, medical, psychiatric, counselling).
 Provide input to supportive housing staff, counsellors, and other professionals regarding program plans.
 Deliver life skills training such as meal preparation, housekeeping, personal care, self-management, and financial literacy (budgeting, rent payments, coordination with Public Trustee).
 Support tenant participation in on-site and off-site programming, including life skills, wellness, and recreational activities.
 Encourage tenant involvement in decision-making related to housing and support practices.
 Provide transition support for tenants moving into or out of Pacifica Housing properties.
 Advocate for tenants experiencing oppression, stigmatization, or discrimination in the community.
 Health, Wellness & Crisis Response 
 Monitor tenant mental health and substance use, identifying when additional support is needed.
 Recognize, analyze, and respond to emergencies, including overdose response and naloxone administration.
 Provide support to tenants with health-related needs, including end-of-life care.
 Liaise and coordinate with community resources such as Assertive Community Treatment (ACT) teams, health practitioners, police, emergency services, and other external supports.
 Community Engagement & Programs 
 Supervise and support tenant participation in community volunteer programs.
 Assist with the food access program to ensure tenants have reliable access to nutritious meals.
 Foster opportunities for tenants to connect with meaningful activities that build skills and community relationships.
 Property Support 
 Provide direct assistance to tenants preparing for pest control treatments or maintenance/repair activities.
 Perform light maintenance and minor repairs (e.g., changing light bulbs) as required.
 Administration & Reporting 
 Maintain up-to-date case notes, tenant records, statistics, and logbooks.
 Prepare incident reports for staff follow-up and Health & Safety Committee review.
 Participate in case management, identifying potential challenges and reporting concerns.
 Assist Team Leads with developing protocols, policies, procedures, and proposals.
 Contribute to fundraising, public relations campaigns, workshops, and special events as required.
 Collaboration & Teamwork 
 Provide backup support for site staff and maintain regular communication with team members.
 Participate in interdisciplinary team meetings, case conferences, and community partner discussions.
 Contribute to a safe, respectful, and inclusive housing environment through teamwork and professional communication.
 Other Duties as Required 
 Carry out related responsibilities that support tenants, programs, and the organization’s mission.
 Engage in organizational initiatives, staff training, and community events.
 Qualifications (minimum Education and Experience requirements):       
 Note :  An equivalent combination of education and experience may be considered. 
 Education: 
 Training and/or education in a related human/social service field is an asset 
 Conflict resolution/crisis prevention training and experience is an asset
 Experience: 
 Recent and related experience preferably in the non-profit housing sector or in a related social service field
 Demonstrated experience working successfully with populations impacted by homelessness, addictions, mental health issues and/or other barriers to stable housing
 Training and/or experience in conflict resolution/crisis prevention
 Knowledge, Skills and Abilities: 
 Knowledge of the psychosocial rehabilitation model
 Demonstrated ability to work independently and be part of an integrated community team
 Knowledge of and belief in the value of harm reduction and “Housing First” theory and practices
 Demonstrated conflict management/crisis prevention skills
 Demonstrated ability to manage and balance role responsibilities and interpersonal dynamics in a fast paced, high pressure environment
 Proficient in MS Office programs including Word, Outlook and Excel 
 General proficiency using a mobile phone to e-mail, text, call and manage calendar appointments
 Additional Criteria for Role: 
 Completion of a Criminal Record Check with the Vulnerable Sector is required before employment commences.
 First Aid Certification is required.
 Naloxone administration training is required. 
 Must have valid driver’s license and access to a reliable vehicle with a minimum of $2 million liability ‘business class’ insurance.

Any offer of employment is contingent on the applicant providing proof of criminal record check prior to commencing employment. 
 Please note: While this position is posted externally concurrently, members within the collective bargaining unit will receive first consideration in the appointment. 
 A mission driven and meaningful working environment.
 Competitive salary from a Certified Living Wage Employer.
 Minimum six (6) percent vacation accrual rate for all regular employees

 Employee assistance program.
 Wellness time.

 Organization and individual training opportunities.

 Dog friendly offices.

 Company Overview  
 Founded in 1943, Auto Electric Service is one of Saskatchewan's largest locally owned and operated automotive parts distributors, proudly serving the automotive aftermarket, agricultural, industrial, heavy-duty and retail sectors throughout Southern Saskatchewan. 
 Our success has been built on strong relationships, industry expertise, dependable service and a commitment to finding solutions for our customers. With a growing distribution network, investments in technology and inventory capabilities, and an ambitious vision for the future, AES is entering an exciting stage of growth. 
 We believe in being Solution Focused, Customer Experience Obsessed, Humbly Confident and keeping our Foot on the Accelerator.
 Position Summary  
 The Business Development Partner is responsible for driving profitable sales growth by identifying, pursuing and securing new customers while building strong, lasting relationships with existing accounts. 
 This is a highly independent, field-focused position where new business development is the primary measure of success. 
 Working closely with the Director of Business Development – Agriculture & Industrial, the Weyburn/Estevan team and our broader sales organization, you will identify opportunities, understand customer operations, recommend solutions and convert prospects into long-term AES customers. 
 You'll represent AES throughout the region, connecting with agricultural producers and businesses, industrial operations, repair facilities, fleet operators and other commercial customers. 
 You'll be more than a salesperson. You'll be a trusted business partner who understands what customers need and takes ownership of delivering results. 
 New Business Development & Customer Acquisition  
 Your primary focus: find opportunities and turn them into business. 
 Proactively identify, prospect and pursue new business opportunities throughout Weyburn, Estevan and surrounding communities.  
 Consistently conduct cold calls, in-person visits and prospecting activities to establish relationships with potential customers.
 Build and maintain a strong pipeline of qualified prospects across the Agriculture, Industrial and Automotive sectors.  
 Identify key decision-makers, understand purchasing needs and develop strategies to win their business. 
 Convert prospects into active, repeat-purchasing customers through consistent follow-up and solution-based selling.  
 Demonstrate persistence, creativity and determination when overcoming objections and competitive barriers. 
 Customer Relationships & Account Growth - Earn trust, deliver value and become the supplier customers want to work with.  
 Develop lasting relationships with existing customers through regular contact, dependable follow-through and exceptional service. 
 Identify opportunities to increase customer purchases, introduce additional product categories and grow AES's share of business.  
 Understand each customer's operation, challenges, purchasing patterns and future requirements.  
 Respond promptly to customer concerns and work collaboratively with internal teams to deliver solutions. 
 Build customer loyalty through integrity, reliability and a genuine commitment to their success. 
   Market Development & Product Opportunities - Know your territory, recognize opportunities and help AES grow.  
  Develop a strong understanding of the agricultural, industrial and automotive businesses operating throughout the territory.  
 Identify underserved markets, competitor weaknesses and emerging customer needs. 
 Gather insights about product demand, seasonal purchasing patterns and potential new product opportunities. 
 Collaborate with the Director of Business Development and Product teams to identify products and solutions that will help AES win new customers.  
 Represent AES professionally at customer locations, industry events and relevant business networking opportunities.

 Take ownership of achieving individual sales growth, new customer acquisition and gross profit objectives.  
 Maintain an organized and active sales pipeline with clear next steps and consistent follow-up. 
 Prepare customer proposals, quotations and account development plans. 
 Use CRM and sales reporting tools to document opportunities, activities and results. 
 Understand pricing, profitability and the importance of generating sustainable business. 
 Manage your territory effectively, prioritizing activities that produce measurable results. 
 Collaborate with store, purchasing, logistics and customer service teams to ensure commitments to customers are consistently met. 
 Key Performance Indicators  
 Success in this role will be measured through a combination of sales activity, customer acquisition, profitable growth and relationship development. Key measures will include: 
 New Customers Acquired: Number of new, active, purchasing customers. 
 New Business Revenue: Sales generated from newly acquired customers. 
 Gross Profit Growth: Profitable sales growth within the assigned territory. 
 Qualified Sales Pipeline: Number and value of active new business opportunities. 
 Prospecting Activity: New customer contacts, cold calls, appointments and follow-up activity. 
 Customer Conversion: Progression of qualified prospects into repeat-purchasing customers. 
 Existing Customer Growth & Retention: Increased purchasing activity and strong customer relationships. 
 Specific targets will be established with the Director of Business Development. 
 Core Competencies 
 Relentless Drive & Determination 
 You are self-motivated, persistent and energized by achieving ambitious goals. Rejection doesn't discourage you; it motivates you to find another approach. 
 Confident Prospecting & Business Development 
 You are comfortable introducing yourself, opening conversations, making cold calls and building relationships from the ground up. 
 Relationship Building & Customer Focus 
 You build trust, listen carefully and understand that exceptional customer experiences are essential to long-term success. 
 Entrepreneurial Mindset 
 You recognize opportunities, take initiative and don't wait to be told what to do. You approach your territory as a business you are responsible for growing. 
 Accountability & Follow-Through 
 You take ownership of your commitments, manage your time effectively and consistently deliver on what you promise. 
 Problem Solving & Adaptability 
 You enjoy challenges, think creatively and find practical solutions that benefit both customers and AES.

 Proven success in outside sales, business development, territory management or relationship-based business-to-business sales.

 Strong communication, negotiation and interpersonal skills. 
 Comfortable working independently and managing a territory with minimal day-to-day supervision. 
 Ability to learn technical products and translate customer needs into practical solutions.

 Valid driver's license and willingness to travel regularly throughout the assigned territory.

 Our AES Core Values

 SOLUTION FOCUSED — We don't dwell on problems. We solve them! You approach obstacles with curiosity, creativity and a commitment to finding the best solution. 
 CUSTOMER EXPERIENCE OBSESSED — Every interaction matters! You recognize that exceptional service builds customer loyalty and creates opportunities for future business.

You take initiative, pursue opportunities with energy and maintain momentum until results are achieved.

 À propos du poste 
 Le ou la gestionnaire principal(e), Pharmacovigilance et sécurité des médicaments assure un leadership stratégique et opérationnel des programmes de pharmacovigilance (PV) et de sécurité des produits de McKesson Canada. Relevant du directeur/trice, Pharmacovigilance corporative et sécurité des médicaments, cette personne dirige une équipe de professionnels de la pharmacovigilance et veille au respect des exigences canadiennes et internationales applicables en matière de sécurité des médicaments.
 Vous superviserez les systèmes et processus de pharmacovigilance, les rapports réglementaires, la gestion des risques, la préparation aux inspections, la surveillance des partenaires d’affaires ainsi que l’amélioration continue pour les médicaments, les produits de santé naturels, les instruments médicaux et autres produits de santé réglementés. Vous contribuerez également à faire progresser les technologies de pharmacovigilance, l’automatisation et l’utilisation responsable de l’intelligence artificielle afin d’améliorer la qualité, la conformité et l’efficacité opérationnelle.
 Vos responsabilités 
 Diriger la mise en œuvre et l’amélioration continue de la stratégie de pharmacovigilance et de sécurité des médicaments de McKesson Canada, ainsi que de son cadre de gouvernance, de ses processus et de son modèle opérationnel.
 Diriger, encadrer et développer une équipe de professionnels de la pharmacovigilance, en établissant les priorités, les attentes en matière de rendement, les plans de ressources et les possibilités de développement.
 Assurer la conformité aux règlements, lignes directrices et normes de l’industrie applicables de Santé Canada et des autorités réglementaires internationales.
 Superviser la gestion des cas de pharmacovigilance, l’examen médical, la qualité des données de sécurité, les rapports réglementaires, la détection et la gestion des signaux ainsi que les activités d’évaluation du rapport bénéfice-risque.
 Superviser l’élaboration et la mise à jour des plans de gestion des risques (PGR), des mesures de minimisation des risques et des rapports périodiques de sécurité.
 Diriger la préparation aux inspections et aux audits de pharmacovigilance, notamment les inspections de Santé Canada, les audits internes et externes, la surveillance de la conformité, les auto-inspections ainsi que l’élaboration des mesures correctives et préventives (CAPA) et la vérification de leur efficacité.
 Établir et surveiller les mesures de conformité et de rendement en pharmacovigilance, les indicateurs clés de performance (KPI), les rapports de gestion et les tableaux de bord.

 POSITION OVERVIEW 
 BDC Capital is seeking an experienced investment professional to join its Growth Venture Fund as a Partner.
 The Growth Venture Fund is a $500 million fund focused on backing and scaling innovative, high-growth Canadian companies with the potential to become national and global category leaders. The Fund makes minority growth equity investments, typically ranging from $15 million to $40 million, in companies with $10 million or more in annual revenue, generally from Series B onward. The Fund invests across industries, targeting differentiated, capital-efficient businesses with strong commercial traction, scalable business models and significant growth potential.
 The Growth Venture Fund team currently manages a portfolio of 28 active late-stage companies.
 Reporting to the Managing Partner, the successful candidate will play a key role in originating, evaluating, executing and managing investments, while contributing to the Fund’s investment strategy, portfolio development and overall performance. The Partner will oversee investment processes, exercise independent investment judgement, and lead investment recommendations to senior leadership and the Investment Committee.
 The Partner will be expected to bring demonstrated experience developing investment opportunities within defined sectors, together with the ability to build expertise, relationships and investment conviction in new and evolving markets.
 While experience in robotics, automation, autonomous technologies, enterprise software, artificial intelligence or consumer businesses would be valuable, greater emphasis will be placed on investment judgment, sector development capabilities, relationship building and demonstrated track record of successful investing than on prior specialization in any particular industry.
 The ideal candidate combines strong commercial judgment, a proven investment track record, established industry relationships and the ability to provide strategic oversight and guidance to investment professionals while working effectively with founders, management teams and other investment stakeholders.
 CHALLENGES TO BE MET 
 Investment Strategy and Origination 
 Take a leadership role in defining and executing the Fund’s investment strategy within a designated sector of expertise.
 Develop and maintain a strong pipeline of attractive investment opportunities through proactive sourcing, market mapping and relationship development.
 Leverage established networks of entrepreneurs, venture capital and growth equity investors, industry executives, advisors and other ecosystem participants.
 Identify companies with differentiated competitive positions, proven business models, attractive growth prospects and the potential to become category leaders.
 Develop informed perspectives on industry dynamics, emerging trends, competitive landscapes and market opportunities.
 Collaborate with other Partners to assess investment opportunities and contribute to portfolio construction across the Fund.
 Investment Evaluation and Execution 
 Lead investment transactions throughout the full investment lifecycle, from initial assessment through due diligence, structuring, negotiation and closing.
 Direct and oversee comprehensive commercial, financial, operational and, where relevant, technical due diligence conducted by investment professionals and external advisors.
 Evaluate market opportunity, competitive differentiation, management capabilities, unit economics, capital requirements, growth potential and investment risks.
 Critically assess investment opportunities, challenging key assumptions, evaluating risks and ensuring the quality and rigor of the investment analysis.
 Review and challenge financial analyses, valuations, investment scenarios and return assessments prepared by investment professionals, providing strategic direction and oversight.
 Lead the formulation of investment recommendations and present them to senior leadership and the Investment Committee, articulating the investment thesis, expected returns, key risks and value creation opportunities.
 Lead the structuring and negotiation of minority equity investments, including primary and secondary transactions, in collaboration with management teams, co-investors and advisors.
 Oversee transaction execution, ensuring effective coordination of internal teams, external advisors and other stakeholders.
 Portfolio Management and Value Creation 
 Take an active role in portfolio company oversight, including participation on boards of directors and relevant board committees.
 Build constructive, trusted relationships with founders, CEOs and management teams.
 Provide strategic guidance on growth initiatives, market expansion, organizational development, capital allocation, financing strategies and other critical business decisions.
 Monitor portfolio company performance, identify emerging risks and opportunities, and recommend appropriate actions.
 Lead or contribute to follow-on financings, strategic transactions and exit planning.
 Leverage BDC Capital’s network and resources to support portfolio companies in achieving their strategic objectives.
 Fund Leadership and Team Development 
 Contribute to the Fund’s investment decisions, portfolio construction, risk management and overall financial performance.
 Work closely with the Managing Partner and other investment professionals to maintain a disciplined and consistent investment approach.
 Mentor and develop junior investment professionals, fostering strong analytical capabilities, sound investment judgment and professional growth.
 Support a collaborative, high-performance team culture characterized by accountability, intellectual rigor and constructive debate.
 Represent the Growth Venture Fund and BDC Capital with entrepreneurs, investors, industry stakeholders and the broader Canadian investment community.
 WHAT WE ARE LOOKING FOR

 Demonstrated track record of sourcing, leading and executing investments in high-growth businesses, preferably at the growth or later venture stages.
 Proven ability to independently manage complex investment transactions, including due diligence, valuation, structuring and negotiation.
 Experience managing investment portfolios, serving on boards of directors and supporting companies through significant growth and strategic transitions.
 Established relationships within the Canadian venture capital and growth investment ecosystem, complemented by relevant international networks.
 Demonstrated ability to generate proprietary investment opportunities and develop strong relationships with founders, executives and investment partners.
 Experience evaluating investment performance, managing portfolio risks and contributing to successful investment outcomes.
 Sector Expertise

 Strong understanding of industry dynamics, competitive positioning, business models and the key drivers of growth and value creation.

 Intellectual curiosity and adaptability, with the ability to develop investment conviction in emerging technologies, evolving industries and unfamiliar markets.

 Investment and Leadership Competencies 
 Investment judgment: Strong analytical and commercial capabilities, with a demonstrated ability to identify attractive risk-adjusted investment opportunities and make sound decisions under uncertainty.
 Strategic thinking: Ability to develop differentiated investment perspectives and translate industry knowledge into actionable investment strategies.
 Financial expertise: Advanced understanding of financial analysis, valuation, investment structuring, portfolio management and return optimization.
 Deal leadership: Proven ability to originate opportunities, manage complex processes, negotiate effectively and execute transactions successfully.
 Relationship management: Ability to establish credibility and trusted relationships with entrepreneurs, management teams, co-investors and other stakeholders.

 Education and Professional Qualifications

We help employees grow professionally; we have a ton of onboarding resources, tutorials, hackathons and buddies to support learnings and provide opportunities to innovate. We have a range of experience levels on teams which allows for mentor/mentee opportunities. Leaders at Jobber work with empathy and support employees to build healthy work-life harmony. Bring your dedication and passion to this job to fulfill your goals.


The team:


Similar to how Jobber empowers small businesses with the tools and insights they need to succeed, the Strategy and Analytics Department ensures our people at Jobber have the tooling, data insights, and strategic direction to excel in our shared mission. We turn data into actionable insights, and critical business needs into impactful software, working with multiple teams and departments across the company. Strategy & Analytics serves as a central hub that drives business outcomes in all corners of Jobber's ecosystem.

Within that department, Data Science is the predictive and prescriptive arm. We're a small, hungry team with an outsized footprint. We work in two-week sprints, demo to the whole department, and expect each other to bring a point of view rather than a ticket.

SignalGraph is our next major project: a company-wide metric graph that connects organizational activity and outcomes so teams can trace metric movement to root causes, investigate faster, and make better decisions.


The role:

Reporting to the Manager, Data Science, the Staff Data Scientist, Applied Machine Learning will own models and systems for automated decisioning. You will train and evaluate models using techniques such as graph representation learning, transformer architectures, and ranking, and engineer them to serve reliably in real time and at scale inside Jobber's product.



This is a senior individual contributor role with strong architectural scope. You'll be the person who decides how ML systems at Jobber are built, evaluated, and trusted and you'll be doing it against a dataset most companies our size don't have: high-velocity SaaS event data, scheduling data, and payments data across hundreds of thousands of service professionals and millions of their clients, plus a rich body of unstructured sales and support text.


The Staff Data Scientist, Applied Machine Learning will:


 - Continue building, improving, and maintaining SignalGraph: evolve metric-family contracts, keep segment and causal-edge catalogs trustworthy, operate the Neo4j and series-refresh pipeline, and strengthen investigation diagnostics so teams can trace metric changes to root causes and make faster decisions from governed evidence..
   

 - Design, build, and evaluate retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) systems on top of that graph. You’ll own retrieval quality, context management, and the evaluation harness that proves the system is actually right, not just fluent.
   

 - Own production ML end-to-end: training pipelines, real-time serving, monitoring, drift detection, and retraining. When a model is live, its uptime, latency, and accuracy are yours.
   

 - Establish systematic evaluation and regression testing as a standard for the team — so model and LLM system quality is measured and defended over time rather than assessed once at launch.
   

 - Set the technical bar and multiply the team: drive MLOps and ML engineering standards, shape our feature store and platform roadmap, review peers' work, and mentor other scientists on graph and deep learning methods.
   

 - Partner directly with senior leadership. Much of what you build will be used by Senior Leaders, Customer Analytics, Business Intelligence, and Product to make decisions against Jobber's North Star goals. You'll present your own work, defend your assumptions, and help cross-functional partners reframe how they approach a problem.
   

 - Stay current, and bring it back. We expect this role to be the most informed person at Jobber on developments in AI/ML methodologically, not just as a consumer of tools, and to translate that into shipped capability.


To be successful, you should have:


 - Production ML experience, end-to-end. You've trained, deployed, served, and maintained models that acted on real users (not just scored offline) You've learned the hard lessons about retraining, drift, and technical debt that come with it.
   

 - A strong statistics foundation. You can reason about bias and variance, justify a loss function, and tell signal from noise without hand-waving.
   

 - Expert SQL and production-grade Python skills. 
   

 - Depth in modern ML methods: Deep learning and neural architectures, transformers/BERT-family models, RNN/CNN, ranking, and representation learning, with hands-on experience applying LLMs in production systems, including RAG and context management.
   

 - Experience designing for the real cost of being wrong. You've built or tuned custom and asymmetric loss functions where a miss in one direction is far more expensive than the other, and you can explain the business reasoning behind the choice.
   

 - Experience with large data in production environments and the platforms that support it. ML/AI platforms such as Snowflake, orchestration with Apache Airflow, and cloud infrastructure (AWS strongly preferred; GCP or Azure equivalent considered).
   

 - Strong communication and stakeholder alignment skills. This team's work only lands if everyone shares the same understanding of what the data means. You can take a room of technical and non-technical partners from confusion to alignment, present uncertainty honestly, and influence without authority.
   

 - Ownership of quality over shipping speed alone. You want to know why something works and how to make it better. You don't accept a model's current performance as its ceiling, and you don't outsource your understanding of your own code to an AI assistant.


It would be nice if you had:


 - Graph experience: Graph theory, graph neural networks, knowledge graphs, or graph databases such as Neo4j. Rare, and the single most valuable thing you could bring to this role.
   

 - A software engineering background: Services and model serving (REST/gRPC), Docker/Kubernetes, CI/CD, feature stores.
   

 - Experience with Snowflake, including Snowpark and Snowpark Container Services, or a comparable path from warehouse to deployed model.

 - Experience building LLM evaluation infrastructure, safety layers, or LLMOps for customer-facing AI.
   

 - Exposure to risk, fraud, or fintech modelling, or to recommendation and ranking systems at scale.

As the Privacy and AI Program Manager, you will operationalize the evolution of our privacy program to encompass the rapidly changing landscape of artificial intelligence. With a customer base that includes a significant portion of the Fortune 1000 and major multinationals, you will ensure our data governance strategies provide uncompromising security, ethical handling, and compliance for highly sensitive information at global scale.

 - Education & Experience: 4+ years of blended experience managing global privacy programs (GDPR, CCPA) within a B2B Enterprise SaaS environment, including direct exposure to AI/ML data governance.

 - Regulatory Competency: Core understanding of current data protection laws and emerging frameworks (including the EU AI Act and automated decision making legislation), with the ability to operationalize these rules without slowing down the pace of development.

 - Technical Fluency: Solid understanding of data flows, cloud infrastructure, and AI models, enabling you to confidently collaborate with engineering teams on system design.

 - Cross-Functional Influence: Strong communication skills geared toward building productive working relationships with technical, legal, and commercial stakeholders.

 - Agile Problem Solving: A scrappy, roll-up-your-sleeves mentality with a proven track record of finding practical, scalable solutions to novel compliance challenges.

 Our platform core is already ~98% built on the web, and we are now expanding our mobile surface. We are looking for an elite Senior React Native Engineer to lead the engineering of our iOS and Android mobile apps from development builds through app store distribution.
 The Mission
 In our ecosystem, fluid animations and instant responsiveness are not cosmetic afterthoughts—they are the core product. We need a mobile engineer who treats 60fps as the bare minimum, understands native thread architecture, and has built complex, gesture-driven unboxing flows on production mobile devices.
 Note: Pure React web experience or wrapper-based webviews will not fit this role. You must have shipped and maintained native mobile builds on the App Store and Google Play.

 High-Dopamine Mobile Mechanics: Write clean, modular TypeScript to architect tactile, gesture-driven interactions—such as mystery pack tears, loot-box carousel reveals, card flips, and real-time drop tickers—using React Native Reanimated , Gesture Handler , and Skia .
 Frame-Rate & Native Performance: Hunt down and eliminate thread bottlenecks, dropped frames, sluggish view hierarchies, and memory leaks across both iOS (iPhones/iPads) and Android (high-end to budget hardware).
 Resilient Data Layer: Build out resilient mobile query pipelines with GraphQL and TanStack Query , handling optimistic cache updates, pagination, network dropouts, and reconnection reconciliation during live unboxings.

 Native Bridges & New Architecture: Leverage React Native’s New Architecture (Fabric, TurboModules) and wire up custom native modules or haptics where JavaScript bridges hit performance limits.
 Shipped Native Mobile Track Record: Strong production experience building and maintaining cross-platform mobile apps in React Native and TypeScript, with direct involvement in apps shipped to both the Apple App Store and Google Play .
 Animation & Gesture Fluency: Deep, hands-on production experience with React Native Reanimated (worklets, shared values) and Gesture Handler . Experience with Shopify React Native Skia or custom canvas shaders is a major advantage.
 Mobile Performance Profiling: Ability to profile real devices using Xcode Instruments, Android Studio Profiler, and React Native DevTools to diagnose UI/JS thread contention and excessive memory footprints.
 State & Network Resilience: Hands-on mastery of GraphQL and TanStack Query (React Query) for managing client caching, race conditions, mutations, and offline/reconnection state handling on unstable mobile connections.
 Dual-Platform Release Knowledge: Practical experience managing builds and submissions through both Apple App Store Connect and the Google Play Console , as well as configuring crash monitoring (Sentry) and over-the-air (OTA) updates.

 High-Growth Ecosystem: The financial backing and operational stability of a proven 2024 parent operator paired with the impact of rolling out a brand-new native mobile app.
 100% Remote: Flexible, asynchronous work environment centered on shipped features and smooth mobile experiences.

 - Own renewal for the segment and flag expansion opportunities from product usage and health data.

 - Build and iterate Float's Scaled CX playbook with leaders across CX, Product, Lifecycle Marketing, and RevOps.

 - Partner beyond scaled onboarding, lifecycle communications, and tech-touch success plans that lift engagement and cut churn.

 - Project-manage cross-functional CX programs, balancing consistency with execution.

 - Work with RevOps and Data on churn prediction models, dashboarding, and customer insights.

 - Test and recommend new tooling to improve digital engagement and success visibility.


CROSS-FUNCTIONAL COLLABORATION

 - Push for the cross-team SLAs and feedback loops that make tech-touch CX actually work.




ABOUT YOU


HERE'S WHAT SETS YOU UP FOR SUCCESS AT FLOAT:

 - You Put Customers First, Always. You care deeply about delivering meaningful value, and you extend that instinct to a book of 7,000 rather than a handful of named accounts.

 - You Act Like an Owner. You take responsibility for outcomes even when most of your book never talks to you directly, and you build the systems that make that ownership possible.

 - You Think Big and Move Fast. You're energized by building from 0 to 1. Float's Scaled segment doesn't have a playbook yet, and you're not waiting for someone else to write it.

 - You Constantly Learn and Grow. You're hungry to improve your craft and open to feedback. You bring a growth mindset to everything you do.

 - You Raise the Bar. You balance the speed a tech-touch motion demands with the rigor a health score and an NRR number both have to hold up to.

 - You Win as a Team. You're a generous collaborator across CX, Product, and RevOps. You lift others up and help make the team stronger.

You've owned a scaled book of business or run 1-to-many success programs across the lifecycle.
   
   - Nice to haves:
     
     - Experience in fintech, payments, or accounting-adjacent products
     
     - Experience building or tuning churn prediction models with a Data or RevOps team

 - You're a builder. You bring a customer- and product-driven mindset that prioritizes both client satisfaction and scale, with a strong orientation toward continuous improvement, feedback loops, and digital CX automation suited to a self-serve or product-led growth environment.

 - You know how to leverage data. Strong proficiency with data analytics and CRM tools to monitor customer health, pull out actionable insight, and measure what a playbook or program actually did across a one-to-many motion.

 - You understand the commercial side. You've owned renewals and expansion at scale, centred on NRR, and can turn customer needs into a business outcome without a name-by-name relationship to lean on.

 - You communicate well. Strong communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to build and hold relationships with customers at every level of an organization, even at a distance.

 - You solve problems. Excellent problem-solving and analytical skills to address customer needs and concerns at scale.




THIS MAY NOT BE THE ROLE FOR YOU IF:

The Opportunity 
 As a Software Developer, you'll design, build, and ship features across our platforms. You'll work closely with product owners, QA, and support to take well-scoped requirements from design through to production, and you'll have real input into how those requirements get shaped in the first place. We're rebuilding our engineering practices as we scale post-acquisition, so you'll help set the standard for code quality, review, and release process — not just follow one that's already fixed in stone.
What Success Looks Like 
 During your first year, you'll: 
 Ship a meaningful body of production code across platforms.
 Build a track record of reliable, well-tested releases with minimal regressions.
 Partner effectively with product owners, QA, and support across the full SDLC.
 Debug and resolve production issues efficiently, with clear root-cause analysis.
 Contribute ideas that improve our engineering practices as we scale.
What You'll Do 
 Design, build, test, and ship features across the platforms.
 Write clean, maintainable code and participate actively in code review.
 Debug and resolve production issues, partnering with support and QA as needed.
 Work closely with product owners to clarify requirements and flag technical tradeoffs early.
 Follow and help improve our SDLC practices (branching, review, release, QA).
 Participate in technical design discussions and architecture decisions for your area.
Why This Role Matters 
 Every feature our operators rely on — bookings, payments, waivers, reporting — is only as good as the engineering behind it. As we rebuild our product organization post-acquisition, the developers who join now will shape not just what gets built, but how reliably and how well it's built for years to come.
 You'll Thrive Here If... 
 You want ownership over how you solve a problem, not just a ticket to close.
 Accountability motivates you.
 You appreciate direct feedback because it helps you improve.
 You like experimenting, learning, and helping build better ways of working.
 You care as much about your teammates' success as your own.
 You want to help build something, not simply inherit it
 Our Hiring Process 
 We believe hiring should be thoughtful, transparent, and fast. Our process typically includes:
 Introductory conversation
 Hiring manager interview
 Technical assessment / pairing exercise
 Leadership conversations
 Final decision
Join Us 
 We're building more than a codebase. We're building the engineering foundation that will define the next chapter of Clubspeed and Resova. If you're looking for a place where you'll be trusted with real ownership over your work, and rewarded for the outcomes you drive, we'd love to hear from you.
 What We're Looking For 
 We're far more interested in judgment, ownership, and coachability than checking every box.
 You'll likely be successful if you have:
 3+ years of professional software development experience, ideally in SaaS or a high-growth product company.
 Comfort working across the full SDLC — from requirements through code review to release and support.
 Strong debugging and problem-solving skills, and the discipline to write tests that hold up in production.
 Clear communication with non-technical stakeholders when clarifying requirements.
 A bias toward shipping: you'd rather get a well-scoped version live and iterate than wait for perfect.
 A commitment to iterative development: you build for today with tomorrow in mind, favoring designs and architecture decisions that stay easy to change as requirements evolve.
 The ability to pivot quickly as market needs shift, implementing sound design decisions in both code and SDLC process.
Technical Requirements 
 We run on two distinct architectures, so the specific stack depends on which product area you join. You'll likely draw on some combination of:

 Deep expertise in any one of these isn't required — comfort moving between modern cloud-native services and established on-prem/monolithic systems matters more than prior experience with our exact stack.

 THE PURPOSE OF YOUR ROLE 
 The Strategic Finance Analyst is a core contributor to Actionstep’s Finance team. The role’s initial focus areas are core FP&A work, including forecasting and profitability analysis; gross margin and pricing analysis; and commission calculations across Sales, Partner, and Operations teams. You will report to the VP of Finance and work closely with the broader Finance and RevOps teams. As Actionstep’s needs evolve, the specific mix of responsibilities may shift, and you may take on additional or different analytical work over time. 
 ABOUT YOU 
 You are a strong finance analyst who thinks in numbers first, and you’re just as comfortable in the data and systems behind those numbers as you are in a spreadsheet. You build clean, reliable models and analysis, and you understand that the work behind a recurring deliverable has to be right every time, not most of the time. 
 You bring real curiosity to the business behind the numbers. You do not just produce an analysis, you ask what it means and whether it should change how the business plans or decides.  
 You move comfortably between recurring, deadline-driven deliverables and more open-ended strategic analysis, and you know how to prioritize when both compete for your time. 
 You build trust across Finance and other teams by being accurate, responsive, and clear about what your analysis does and does not say. You take feedback well and ask questions up front rather than guessing. 
 WHAT YOU WILL BE DOING 
 The focus areas below reflect the business’s current priorities. As with most roles on a growing team, they may change as those priorities evolve, and may also include support for strategic initiatives such as partnerships or M&A as they arise. 
 FP&A: Forecasting & Profitability 
 Support the development and maintenance of annual budgets and rolling forecasts. 
 Conduct budget-to-actual variance analysis and support profitability analysis across the business. 
 Build and maintain financial models to support business decisions, including scenario and sensitivity analysis, particularly through the use of AI tools. 
 Contribute datasets and analysis to board and executive reporting materials. Work closely with other members of the Finance team, including the Senior Financial & Systems Analyst, on shared data and reporting priorities. 
 Pricing & Gross Margin Analysis 
 Conduct gross margin analysis by product, segment, and customer cohort, and identify trends and margin improvement opportunities. 
 Support pricing strategy and annual price increase analysis, including modeling impact across customer segments, for new and existing product lines. 
 Partner with Billing and RevOps to validate pricing and margin data before it reaches leadership. 
 Commission Calculations 
 Support monthly/quarterly commission calculations for Sales, Partner, and Operations teams, including quality control checks prior to distribution. 
 Partner with Sales, RevOps, and Partner teams to ensure the data behind commission calculations, such as bookings, quotas, and contract terms, is accurate. 
 Investigate and resolve commission discrepancies as they arise. 
 Data & Systems 
 Partner with the Senior Financial & Systems Analyst on the data and systems behind the company’s business intelligence, recurring reporting, and general analysis efforts. 
 Automate recurring deliverables, such as commission calculations, to reduce manual, spreadsheet-based work over time. 
 Contribute to the infrastructure work, the “plumbing,” that keeps Finance’s data and systems running reliably via a company-wide data warehouse.

 Build or maintain dashboards and reporting views that support recurring Finance deliverables. 
 Flag data quality issues upstream and work with the relevant team to fix them at the source.

Quantitative Researcher / Signal Generator - Alpha Signal Program
 About us 
 We're a small, elite team of AI researchers and engineers building predictive models across commodities, prediction markets, and global macro. We're well capitalized, we move fast, and we care about one thing above all: whether a signal actually works.
 The Alpha Signal Program is how we bring in talent from outside the usual channels. We've found that the people with real edge aren't always the ones with the right CV or the right address.
 The opportunity
 This isn't a conventional job, and we'd rather be upfront about that. You won't be assigned a desk or a manager. Instead, you bring us a signal — a model, a systematic strategy, a way of reading a market that you believe gives you an edge — and we put real capital behind it. We handle the execution, the risk, and the infrastructure. You're paid a performance fee tied directly to how your signal performs.
 You can do this from anywhere in the world, on your own schedule, alongside whatever else you're doing. If your signal works, the upside is yours to share in. If it doesn't, you've lost nothing but the time it took to find out.
 What you'd be working on
 You'd develop and refine predictive signals in one or more of the following areas:
 Commodities — energy, metals, agriculture, and the relationships between them, physical and financial.
 Prediction markets — event probabilities and mispriced odds, wherever information becomes a price.
 Global macro — rates, FX, sovereign risk, and cross-asset calls, systematic.
 We don't filter on pedigree. You might be a quant, a full-time trader, an academic, or entirely self-taught. What matters is that you can show us a genuine edge and explain why it holds up.
 We're especially keen to hear from:
 Self-directed traders with a verifiable track record but no institutional name behind them
 Researchers from physics, mathematics, engineering, or computer science who apply their tools to markets
 Specialists who understand one corner of the world — a commodity, an energy market, an election — better than the Street does
 Anyone who has been right often enough to know it isn't luck
 A performance fee tied directly to what your signal earns — the stronger and more consistent it is, the larger your share
 Real capital behind your ideas, plus institutional-grade execution and risk management
 Complete flexibility: fully remote, work from anywhere, on your own time
 No relocation, no employment requirement to begin, and no obligation to share anything sensitive before an NDA is in place
 The chance to work alongside a world-class team of AI researchers and engineers who will push your thinking harder than anyone else
 How to apply
 Click apply and attach your supporting material — your CV, a track record, a short description of your signal or approach, or whatever best makes your case. You don't need to give away how your edge works at this stage; we just want a clear picture of who you are and what you bring.
 If it looks promising, we'll be in touch to sign an NDA and take it from there.

Float is on a mission to simplify finance for Canadian businesses, empowering them to eliminate complexity and unlock new opportunities. We openly share our thoughts and differing opinions so we can continue to improve. We do our best to keep our decision-making decentralized so that all team members feel ownership in our success.




OUR PRODUCT

Float is Canada’s intelligent financial operating system, combining modern financial services and software to help businesses spend, save, and grow. Trusted by more than 10,000 Canadian companies, Float provides high-limit corporate cards, automated expense management, next-day bill payments, high-yield accounts, and industry-leading support, all built in Canada, for Canada. Float recently announced our $85 million Series C https://floatfinancial.com/press/float-financial-raises-cad-85-million-series-c, and is backed by world-class investors, including Inovia Capital, Growth Equity at Goldman Sachs Alternatives, OMERS Ventures, and Silicon Valley Bank.

 

Our team is a collection of ambitious, collaborative and mission-driven people from all walks of life but with one goal: helping Canadian companies not just survive but thrive. And we’re looking for bold innovators to help shape the future of business finance in Canada.




AI USE IN OUR HIRING PROCESS

We use technology, including artificial intelligence (AI), to support parts of our hiring process. This may include AI-assisted scheduling and candidate communications, and AI-generated interview notes, guides or summaries to help our team focus on the conversation. All hiring decisions are made by our hiring team.




ABOUT THE ROLE

We're hiring a Senior Product Manager to own the rails that move money into, out of and across Float: financial ledgering, financial accounts, payment rails (EFT, wires, ACH, cross-border and FX) and card infrastructure. Reporting to the GM, Banking, you'll work across three engineering squads to build and maintain the infrastructure behind our corporate cards, payments, FX and banking products. You'll think about the whole life of a payment — how it starts, how its status is communicated, what happens when it fails or is returned, and how customers and our teams resolve exceptions. You'll work with a designer, eight engineers and a product operations specialist focused on analytics and go-to-market planning.



WHAT YOU'LL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR

 - Own the Financial Infrastructure roadmap end to end: sizing, sequencing, delivery, launch and iteration.

 - Make payment health measurable and keep improving it — success rate, processing speed, failure recovery and reconciliation.

 - Evaluate and manage infrastructure partners with our Product Partnerships team, including partner changes and new rail launches.

 - Manage dependencies with banks, networks and processors that move on their own timelines. Escalate risks early, with options attached.

 - Partner closely with Engineering on APIs, data models, ledger interactions, controls and observability.

 - Make trade-off calls across customer experience, speed, reliability, risk, compliance, operational complexity and commercial impact.

 - Coordinate across our card, payments and banking products so infrastructure work supports the whole business.

 - Learn how finance leaders run payroll funding, tax remittance and multi-currency treasury, and work with Design to build accounts, treasury and FX into those workflows.

 - Work with Risk, Compliance, Operations, Finance and GTM from the start, not as approval steps at the end.

 - Keep leadership and partner teams clearly informed across many projects at once.

 - Use AI tools to speed up discovery, analysis, documentation and decision-making.

 - You Put Customers First, Always. You care deeply about delivering meaningful value. Whether you're building internal systems or customer-facing features, you're always thinking about how to make life better for our users.

 - You Act Like an Owner. You take responsibility for outcomes, step up to challenges, and seek solutions proactively—doing what's best for the business, not just your role.

WHAT YOU'LL BRING

IN SHORT
